arxiv-2605-08946: Real decisions trade off competing goals — speed versus safety — and the Pareto front maps the best compromises. arxiv-2605-09046: Robots planning motions under uncertainty must care about where they end up, not just the journey. plos-pone-0003446: Marine biologists rethought how a giant fish swims in this 2008 paper. The ocean sunfish, Mola mola, can weigh two tons and was long dismissed as a drifting plankton-like oddity. plos-pone-0003546: Conservation biologists showed roads redraw elephant maps in this 2008 Congo study. plos-pone-0003646: In 2008, a team found timing matters for a key cell signal in fruit flies. Cells in the bristle lineage answered the Notch pathway best while copying their DNA, the S-phase of the cell cycle. The result shows cells hear the signal best at one point in their own growth round.
plos-pone-0003746: In 2008, Schmid and Yang warned gene hunters about a popular shortcut. Sliding-window scans for selection pressure along proteins can mislead, and their BRCA1 case study shows the trap in action. The cautionary paper urges care with a method many had used on trust.
plos-pone-0003846: In 2008, Sevillano, Aguilar, and Alou tested antibiotics on germ communities, not loners. Their mixed cultures of common respiratory bacteria revealed how beta-lactam drugs shift the nasal ecosystem. The community view better predicts treatment effects than single-germ tests.
plos-pone-0003946: In 2008, Chen, Gottlieb, and Cohen studied DNA's most frozen patches near a brain gene. Ultraconserved elements in the Olig2 promoter were analyzed for their role in myelin-making cells. The work asks why evolution refuses to touch these sequences.
plos-pone-0004046: In 2008, Piao, Lee, and Kim caught a Wnt receptor directly braking a kinase. The phosphorylated cytoplasmic tail of the LRP6 coreceptor inhibited GSK3beta. plos-pone-0004146: In 2009, Martin, Pearson, and Brenneman linked diet to fertility genes. Gonad genes shifted activity with food energy intake. The breeding system sensed the food supply. The study ties food supply to breeding readiness. The mechanism helps explain diet-linked fertility swings.
plos-pone-0004246: In 2009, Wang, Johnston, and Yang traced fungi living inside leaves. The endophytic lifestyle reshaped reproductive structures in leaf fungi. plos-pone-0004346: In 2009, Li and Agarwal mapped human diseases by their wiring. A pathway-based view revealed relationships among human diseases. Shared pathways linked seemingly distant ills. The map could repurpose drugs across diseases today. The work shows diseases are not isolated islands.
plos-pone-0358646: Physics-informed neural networks bake the laws of physics into AI — but they still waste effort on easy regions. plos-pone-0341946: Public attitudes to science aren’t just knowledge versus ignorance. The model moves past the ‘deficit’ idea toward how belief systems actually work.
plos-pone-0352346: North Atlantic right whales are critically endangered, and understanding how they feed is vital to saving them. This paper identified feeding behavior using camera-validated kinematic data and machine learning. The method lets researchers read feeding events straight from motion tags on free-swimming whales.
plos-pone-0358046: Light doesn’t just let us see — different wavelengths reach deep into the brain. plos-pone-0358246: Pancreatic cancer desperately needs finer subtypes to guide treatment. The multi-layer integration sorts tumors far more precisely than any single data type could.
plos-pone-0357346: Coastal forests are retreating under pressure — and satellites can track exactly how fast. This paper mapped coastal forest retreat using convolutional neural networks applied to different satellite imagery. The AI-generated maps give conservationists the retreat’s true extent, free from guesswork.
plos-pone-0357146: Autism evaluations by telehealth are only as good as the internet connection carrying them. This paper studied telehealth autism evaluation under suboptimal network conditions, covering technical parameters and clinical implications. The findings set minimum standards so remote diagnosis stays trustworthy even on bad connections.
plos-pone-0356746: Preterm birth shakes fathers as well as mothers — a fact medicine too often ignores. This study tracked the effects of threatened and actual preterm birth on the course of paternal peripartum depression and anxiety. The fathers’ trajectories demand attention from perinatal care that has focused almost entirely on mothers.
plos-pone-0357446: Ghana’s forests keep falling — to expanding farms and mines. This national-scale assessment showed agricultural expansion and mining drive forest loss even as headline deforestation rates decline. The evidence names the true culprits, giving policymakers nowhere to hide from the data.
plos-pone-0356646: Silver nanoparticles can be brewed green — using plant chemistry instead of toxic reagents. This phytochemical profiling-guided study synthesized and characterized silver nanoparticles using Catunaregam spinosa for biological applications. The green method delivers useful nanomaterials without the poisonous footprint.
plos-pone-0357046: Solving equilibrium problems on a deadline demands dynamical systems with guaranteed timing. This paper developed finite-time and predefined-time dynamical systems for strongly pseudomonotone mixed equilibrium problems. The mathematics converges on a predictable schedule — valuable for real-time applications.
plos-pone-0355946: Physicians suffer chest pain too — and their own risk factors are under-studied. This multinational cross-sectional study measured the prevalence, characteristics, and determinants of chest pain among physicians in the Middle East and North Africa. The findings turn the stethoscope toward the caregivers themselves.
plos-pone-0356146: Culturally loaded words — idioms, allusions, untranslatable concepts — defeat machine translation. This paper combined a diffusion model with sparse coding to improve translation accuracy of such words in English news texts. The hybrid approach finally gives culture its due in MT.
plos-pone-0355846: Iron locked in Indo-Gangetic alluvial soils releases differently as moisture swings. This multi-model kinetic and geochemical speciation study examined iron release dynamics under variable moisture. The insights guide smarter iron fertilization for one of the world’s great breadbaskets.
plos-pone-0356546: Diamond Open Access — free to publish, free to read — promises a fairer scholarly world. The on-the-ground findings reveal what helps and what hinders open publishing in a West African research community.
plos-pone-0318046: Oil palm plantations are biodiversity deserts — but exactly how empty, and can monitoring help? plos-pone-0356246: After liver surgery, neutrophils expressing Cd14 surge in orchestrated waves. This paper used integrated transcriptomic and phenotypic analyses to reveal their spatiotemporal variation after hepatectomy. The immune choreography it mapped could guide interventions that help livers regenerate without destructive inflammation.
plos-pone-0356046: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. The journal has retracted AptaFluorescence — an aptamer-based fluorescent imaging protocol for biomolecule visualization. The notice formally withdraws the protocol from the scientific record.
plos-pone-0337146: Growing white button mushrooms sustainably means recycling what the industry now wastes. plos-pone-0355546: Parental stress reaches children through genes, womb, and home — in different measure. This paper disentangled heritable, prenatal, and environmental pathways of parental stress and their differential influences on children’s effortful control and cortisol regulation. The findings map how stress transmits across generations — and where interventions can break the chain.
plos-pone-0345346: Five days of heat acclimation can transform athletes’ heat tolerance. The findings reassure: rapid heat adaptation is safe for the kidneys — good news as competitions heat up.
plos-pone-0355646: Puerarin — a medicinal plant compound — dissolves poorly, limiting its use. This paper enhanced its solubility via melt sonocrystallization. The improved formulation could unlock the therapeutic potential of a compound traditional medicine has valued for centuries.
plos-pone-0339746: Cutaneous leishmaniasis — disfiguring skin sores — needs better diagnostics. europmc-pmc2795146: Cooling newborns' bodies is used to limit brain damage after oxygen loss at birth, but doctors need to see whether it protects tissue. europmc-pmc2827546: Dental plaque is a structured community, not a random film. This 2010 paper uses advanced microscopy to reveal the architecture of oral biofilms on natural teeth. europmc-pmc2833246: Cancer stem cells thrive in low-oxygen tumor cores, and this 2010 review explains the machinery. The authors survey how hypoxia inducible factors sustain cancer stem cells. europmc-pmc2841246: The enzyme COX-2, famous as the target of painkillers, also shapes cancer. This 2010 review examines its role in cell proliferation and cell death in human malignancies. europmc-pmc2859946: Low oxygen rewires tumor cells, and this 2010 paper traces one wire. europmc-pmc2893946: A little-known T cell spots infected cells by their bacterial scent. This 2010 paper shows human mucosal associated invariant T cells detect bacterially infected cells. The authors reveal a fast innate-like defense. Their discovery added a player to immunity's roster.
europmc-pmc2941746: Cancer cells crawl using molecular motors, and this 2010 review names the drivers. The authors cover Rac and Rho GTPases in cancer cell movement control. europmc-pmc3081346: A microRNA builds tumor blood vessels. This 2011 paper shows MiR-21 spurs vessel growth via AKT, ERK, and HIF-1 signals. The authors map the pathway. Their work points to vessel-starving therapy. Blocking MiR-21 shrank tumors in mice. The pathway is now a drug target.
europmc-pmc6560046: Babies born under 2,500 grams face higher risks of death, stunting, and adult disease - and 2015 saw millions of them. europmc-pmc6627346: Vitamin D shortfalls reach beyond bones - into genes themselves.
